# ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops Weekly Report (Jul 26 - Aug 1, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, the `superchain-ops` repository focused on refining upgrade strategies for interoperable chains and stabilizing CI/CD infrastructure. Significant technical discussions centered on ensuring consistent post-migration OPCM upgrades across chain sets and addressing gas estimation logic for the upcoming Glamsterdam hardfork. While routine maintenance included submodule updates and task executions, the team also pivoted its investigation into persistent flaky tests, identifying potential peer-management defects within the Execution Layer (EL).

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### CI/CD & Infrastructure Maintenance
*   **Submodule Synchronization:** The `superchain-registry` submodule was updated to align with changes following the removal of `sepolia-dev-0`. This update was critical for resolving a CircleCI job failure and ensuring the repository reflects the current state of the Superchain registry ([#1508](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1508)).
*   **Operational Task Execution:** Progress was recorded for operational workflows, specifically confirming the execution and status update of Task 60 ([#1509](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1509)).

### Protocol & Upgrade Strategy
*   **OPCM Upgrade Pathing:** Extensive analysis was conducted on how to handle `OPContractsManager` (OPCM) upgrades for chains within an interoperable set. The team is currently leaning toward an idempotent migration approach (Option 1) that resolves the `ProxyAdmin` during the upgrade. This strategy prioritizes consistent state across all chains in a dependency set over gas efficiency, mitigating the risk of partial upgrades or incompatible contract versions ([#21731](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/21731)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Proposer Instance Management:** The investigation into detecting multiple `kona-sp1-proposer` instances sharing the same key was closed. Maintainers determined the likelihood of this collision is extremely low and the operational impact is minor enough to not warrant further complex detection logic ([#22020](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/22020)).

### Active Issues & Blockers
*   **Glamsterdam Precompile Gas Costs (EIP-8037):** Discussions are ongoing regarding the `PRECOMPILE_CALL_RESERVED_GAS` threshold. Current testing suggests that the existing oracle bytecode may require a significant increase in reserved gas—potentially up to 400,000—to guarantee whole-function completion. The team is deciding between redefining the guard threshold or simply adding regression coverage for Amsterdam gas estimation ([#19380](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/19380)).
*   **EL-Backfill Stalls:** The `TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_CLSync` test family continues to exhibit flakiness. Recent logs indicate the root cause is likely an `op-reth` peer-management defect where the follower fails to re-establish EL peer connections during backfill, leading to a total stall rather than a slow catch-up ([#21041](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/21041)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by deep technical coordination regarding the Superchain's upgradeability architecture. The debate over OPCM migration strategies ([#21731](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/21731)) highlights active collaboration between contributors to balance protocol safety with developer experience. Additionally, the pivot in the flaky test investigation demonstrates a cross-component debugging effort, moving from simple test budget adjustments to identifying deeper defects in the `op-reth` Engine API and peer management.
